figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. (A) The myb gene cluster and gene annotations. (B)
Possible pathway for the biosynthesis of mycobacidin (1). (C) LC-
MS analysis of the reactions catalyzed by the radical SAM enzymes
identified in the genome of the mycobacidin producing strain upon
incubation with 8. (D) LC-MS analysis of the reactions catalyzed by
MybC for the production of 7. (E) LC-MS analysis of the MybD
assays for the production of 8.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Radical SAM enzymes that catalyze sulfur incorporation
into biomolecules include (A) LipA, (B) RimO, (C) MiaB, and (D)
ThnL. [FexSx]: Fe−S clusters in proteins, CAT: catalytic cluster,
AUX: auxiliary cluster; Cbl: cobalamin; the red “S″ represents the
sulfur source in the enzymatic reactions.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. (A) Proposed MybB-catalyzed sulfur insertion reaction with
the bridging sulfur derived from the auxiliary [Fe2S2]AUX cluster. (B)
UV−visible absorbance of as-isolated MybB suggesting the presence
of an [Fe2S2] cluster. (C) Superposition of the structural model of
MybB (blue, predicted by AlphaFold 3.0Beta) and E. coli BioB/SAM
complex (tan, PDB: 1R30) to predict the coordination mode of Fe−S
clusters in the active site of MybB. Coordination residues for the
[Fe4S4]CAT/SAM complex and [Fe2S2]AUX binding are highlighted in
the top and bottom enlarged circles, respectively. (D) LC-MS analysis
of the MybB assay in the presence of the Fe−S scaffold protein IscU
following reconstitution of IscU with either Na2S or Na2
34S to
determine the origin of the bridging sulfur. (E) UV−visible
absorbance spectra monitoring degradation of the [Fe2S2] clusters
in the MybB assay at different time points with a protein
concentration of approximately 75 μM. The spectra were taken
after the reaction samples were exposed to air overnight to decompose
dithionite and the [Fe4S4] cluster. (F) UV−visible absorbance
subtraction spectra monitoring the difference between the spectrum
of the unreacted control and that of the MybB reaction at several time
points over 120 min.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. (A) Biosynthesis of biotin catalyzed by enzymes from biotin
and mycobacidin pathway. (B) LC-MS analysis of the MybB assay
with dethiobiotin (3) as the substrate for biotin maturation. The
reaction was also carried out in the presence of 1 (10 mM, 10-fold)
for comparison. (C) LC-MS analysis of the MybD and MybC assays
with DAPA 23 as the substrate.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. (A) Possible mechanisms of MybB catalyzed 4-thiazolidinone cyclization during mycobacidin biosynthesis. (B) Synthetic probes
thiolated at C7 or C10 were used to explore the catalytic mechanism. (C) LC-MS analysis of MybB-catalyzed enzymatic reactions utilizing probes 32
and 33.
